correctness.rationale: For finite positive nu, coherent-state overlaps give c0>0 and c2>=0, equality only at a point mass located at b. The exact derivatives c0 prime=c1/sqrt2 and c1 prime=c2-c0/sqrt2 cancel the c0 terms in d(c0 squared+c1 squared)/db=2c1c2. Every global Q1 maximum (which exists since coefficients decay) has c1=0, and the Q0 maximum has c1=0 as well, proving equal optima and argmax sets. If nu is not a point mass, c2 positive at an optimum yields strict best degree-two gain. For symmetric atoms +-a, b=a tanh(ab/2) and monotonic tanh(z)/z establish the sharp bifurcation at a=sqrt2. Quadrature, finite differences and finite grids check the constants but do not prove universal quantification.

value.rationale: The all-positive-mixture theorem solves a motivated basis-design decision: optimally moving a Hermite basis wholly absorbs the approximation advantage of the first odd degree, but cannot absorb the positive second degree. It offers an exact and broadly parameterized benchmark distinguishing p-enrichment from translation, and a sharp two-Gaussian optimizer bifurcation; this is a structural approximation fact, not a mere special case or numerical optimization output. Scope is limited to fixed-width L2 Hermite projection, not practical global solver performance.
